intro: Clothes that fit or not, what happens to them in the wash, and the vocabulary of paying and complaining.

palabras.consejo: The «ll» sounds like «y»: «kre-ma-YE-ra». You pull it up and down.
It is also the button on a device, which you press. The plural, «botones», has no accent.
The opposite is «liso». There are fabrics «estampadas» with flowers or other designs.
The «g» sounds like «j»: «en-ko-HER». I «encojo», you «encoges».
It is the opposite of «encoger». A woollen jumper often «da de sí».
The opposite is «estar de moda». It agrees: «una chaqueta pasada de moda».
It is not «cocer», which is cooking. In Spain «coser» has an s sound and «cocer» a th.
It comes from «coser»: «des-» undoes the action. A seam «se descose».
You pay everything at once. The opposite is «a plazos».
A «plazo» is each part of the payment. You can pay a fridge or a car «a plazos».
The «ñ» sounds «ny»: «se-NYAL». It also means a sign or a signal.
It helps you complain. With the «factura» you can ask for an exchange or a refund.
It comes from «consumir». Consumers have a right to a guarantee, exchange and refund.
In Spain every business must have one. You ask for it like this: «una hoja de reclamaciones, por favor».
«la» refers to a feminine noun like «la prenda». «lavarla» means to wash it.
«encogido» comes from «encoger», to shrink. The «g» before «i» sounds like «j»: en-ko-SI-do.
«talla» is feminine: «la talla». The «ll» is pronounced «y»: TA-yas.
Here «la» refers to a feminine item. «llevarla» means to take it somewhere.
«el tinte» is masculine. The «ti» sounds like «ti» in «tip»: TIN-te.

The accent on «pagué» marks the stress at the end: pa-GE. «gu» before «e» sounds «ge».
«guardar» means to keep. The accent on «guardé» marks the last syllable: gwar-DE.
«devolverle» = «devolver» + «le». The stress stays on «BER».
«producto» is masculine: «el producto». The «c» before «t» sounds like «k».
«apretado» means tight. It agrees with «pantalones», which is masculine plural.
The «ie» diphthong is one sound. It follows an idea of wish or doubt.
«estampado» is a printed pattern. The feminine form «estampada» agrees with «chaqueta».
«chasquido» is masculine: «el chasquido». The «ch» is pronounced as in «church».
«cuello» is masculine: «el cuello». The «ll» is «y»: KWE-yo.
«manga» is feminine: «la manga». The «g» before «a» is hard: MAN-gas.
«frunce el ceño» means to frown. The «c» before «e» sounds «th» in Spain.
«prenda» is feminine: «la prenda». It is any single piece of clothing.
«enhebrar» means to thread a needle. The «h» is silent: en-E-bra.
«aguja» is feminine: «la aguja». The «j» is pronounced like a strong «h»: a-GU-ha.
«coger» means to pick up. The «g» before «e» sounds like a strong «h»: KO-he.
«coser» is to sew. It sounds similar to «coger» but means a different action.
«quejarte» means to complain. The «j» sounds like «h»: ke-HAR-te.
Adverbs in «-mente» add «-mente» to the adjective: «oficial» becomes «oficialmente».

piezas.titulo: How it fits, how it is cared for and how it is paid
texto:
**How it fits.** **Quedar** + adjective works like **gustar**: **me queda apretado**, **me quedan grandes**. **Me sienta bien** means it suits me.

**What happens to clothes.** A garment **encoge** in the wash or **da de sí** with use. A seam **se descose** and you **cose** it with needle and thread. Fabric can be plain or **estampada**. If it is no longer worn, it is **pasada de moda**.

**Parts.** **La cremallera**, **los botones**, **el bolsillo**, **la manga**.

**How you pay.** **Al contado** (all at once) or **a plazos** (a part each month). To reserve something, you leave **una señal**. You ask for **la factura** or the receipt.

**How you complain.** The **consumidor** has rights: guarantee, exchange and refund. If there is no solution, you ask for **la hoja de reclamaciones**.

piezas.titulo: Quedar, dar de sí and «preferiría que…»
texto:
**Quedar + adjective** says how a garment fits you. It agrees with the garment, not with you: **este abrigo me queda grande**, **estos pantalones me quedan apretados**.

**Encoger and dar de sí** tell what happens to clothes. With the present perfect: **ha encogido**, **ha dado de sí**.

**Preferiría que + imperfect subjunctive** is a very polite way to ask: **preferiría que me devolvieran el dinero**, **preferiría que me lo cambiaran**.

The imperfect subjunctive of **devolver** is **devolviera**, **devolvieras**, **devolviera**, **devolviéramos**, **devolvierais**, **devolvieran**.

ejemplos.alumno: These trousers are tight on me.
